text: What if the shop came to you? A Korean sweet seller stands before people resting along a street. The broad tray carried on the body acts as a small display counter. Follow the customers eyes and the hands reaching toward the goods. A brief exchange joins someone at work with someone taking a rest. A visitor might ask what was sold and how a person carried the whole shop. The scene describes a way goods reached people. For the seller, it was a working day as well as a curious sight to others. This work is attributed to Uncho. From the TJ Kim Collection, imagine the sweetness and the effort of carrying it through the streets.
